topic.title: Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Language-Model Reasoning
topic.area: Language Models and Natural Language Processing
topic.overview: This topic uses reinforcement learning to improve reasoning while reducing the cost of policy updates and generated trajectories. Methods change advantage estimation, sample selection, behavior preparation, and allocation of training or inference compute. The practical bottleneck is often repeated generation rather than the arithmetic of a parameter update.
topic.whyItMatters: Efficiency improvements can make reasoning training accessible, but fewer rollouts may reduce exploration or bias which problems receive attention. Accuracy, memory, generation cost, and robustness need to be evaluated together.
topic.evolution: The broader collection includes policy gradients for structured domains and memory-assisted program synthesis. Recent representatives focus on reasoning models, with offline value estimation, single-generation updates, prolonged training, and uncertainty-guided sample selection. These alternatives explore how much learning signal each trajectory supplies rather than assuming that more sampled answers always produce proportionate benefits.
openQuestions: Which sample-selection rules preserve difficult but important reasoning cases?
When can offline value estimates replace online exploration without limiting eventual capability?
